title: The overall objective(s) of the guideline is (are) specifically described.

chain_of_thought.step1_locate: Introduction section and key recommendations section
step2_evidence: Diabetes is the leading cause of major complications, such as end-stage renal disease and lower extremity amputations, and is a significant contributor to ischemic heart disease, stroke, peripheral vascular disease, and vision loss (1).

Older adults account for an estimated 60% to 70% of the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) and U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) diabetic population (largely retirees) (VA/DoD. Unpublished data).

Benefits include greater knowledge of medications (13) and understanding of risks (14). In addition, patient-centered care and shared decision making together may decrease patient anxiety, increase trust in clinicians (15), and improve treatment adherence (16).
chain_of_thought.step3_reasoning:
The guideline comprehensively describes:
- Health content: Type 2 diabetes as the disease with specific complications (end-stage renal disease, amputations, cardiovascular issues)
- Target population: Veterans with type 2 diabetes, particularly older adults (60-70% of VA/DoD diabetic population)
- Expected benefits: Reduced complications, improved patient knowledge, decreased anxiety, increased trust, and better treatment adherence through shared decision-making

All three required elements (disease, population, outcomes) are explicitly stated in verbatim text, meeting the criteria for score 7.
